stories.reason: Zero journeys are qualified, which is the whole of this story's exit criterion. CF-P7-017 landed on 2026-07-27 (D-P7-02) and fixed the dispatch bug in the working tree, but the fix has not been observed on a live deployment: Cloudflare Pages binds code at build time, so the existing measured deployment -- built before this fix existed -- cannot show it, and no agent pushed a commit or triggered a new Preview build. Even against a rebuilt deployment, the journeys this story must qualify are signed-in journeys and no OAuth session is available to an agent. The gate cf:phase7:preview:check passes while this story does not, because the gate truthfully asserts a fail-closed deployment and the story needs a qualified journey. A green gate is not a closed story.

qualification.reason: Two independent reasons, one of which changed today. (1) Every collaboration route answered 503 COLLABORATION_UNAVAILABLE on every deployment measured on 2026-07-27, and the cause was in the code, not configuration: functions/_lib/api-shell.mjs returned the same 503 on both branches of its own feature check while functions/_lib/identity/environment.ts read COLLABORATION_ENABLED with the opposite polarity to its name. CF-P7-017 fixed both on 2026-07-27 (D-P7-02) and is now PASS -- but the fix lives in the working tree only. No agent pushed a commit or triggered a new Preview build, and Cloudflare Pages binds code at build time, so the measured deployment above still reflects the pre-fix behaviour and cannot be re-measured to show otherwise without a new build. (2) Independent of the dispatch bug and unaffected by fixing it: the journeys this story must qualify are signed-in journeys, and no OAuth session is available to the agent -- signing in requires entering credentials at github.com, which is prohibited, and no session cookie was issued to or held by this story. Qualification remains an owner-driven exercise.
qualification.not_claimed: No 2xx response from any collaboration route has been observed by this programme on any deployment. Nothing about the on-path is asserted here.
qualification.dispatch_bug_status: FIXED in the working tree by CF-P7-017 (D-P7-02); not yet observed on a deployment because none was rebuilt.

renegotiated.reason: The 60 was written at plan time and read by no script until this gate existed, so it was never derived from a measurement. Meeting it needs a bundling step this project does not have anywhere. 100 was chosen against the measurement rather than from it: set at 91.93 the budget would be unfalsifiable, since the next byte breaches it; set far above, it enforces nothing. Roughly 8 KiB of headroom lets ordinary work proceed and makes another growth of the size this phase saw reach the number and force the conversation again.
renegotiated.not_claimed: The payload did not get smaller and no build step was added. The programme is carrying 91.93 KiB knowingly, at a figure an owner set with the measurement in front of them.

deployment_measurement.measured_against: Preview deployment 681ad3ca-f0f7-4f66-8649-c7dab3de798d as Cloudflare serves it

local_measurement.method: gzip level 9 over every module in the static import closure of js/collaboration/entry.js, with CRLF normalised to LF so the figure is identical on a Windows working copy and in CI. Recomputed by cf:phase7:exit:check on every run; the gate fails if this record and the bytes disagree by more than 2 KiB in either direction, and fails if the measurement drops under the declared budget while this record still says OPEN.
local_measurement.grew_since_prior_reading: CF-P7-013's two mutation journeys (device registration, workspace creation) were wired for the first time this session, adding device-record.js and workspace-key-envelope.js and expanding entry.js. The prior reading (81.74 KiB) measured a chrome that composed these surfaces but could not act on either.

lazy_chunk_budget.narrowest_reading: Excluding the three inherited Phase 5/6 service modules the lazy path also pulls -- device-key-lifecycle.js, outbox.js and conflict-resolution.js -- the nineteen Phase 7 modules alone are 77.88 KiB gzip locally and were 64.3 KiB on the deployment. Against the renegotiated 100 both readings pass; against the original 60 neither did, which is what D-P7-03 weighed.
lazy_chunk_budget.cause: There is no bundling or minification step anywhere in this project. Twenty-two unminified source files are served exactly as authored, comments included. The size is a property of the shape that currently ships, not of a build artifact -- which is why meeting 60 was a build-system change rather than a trim.
lazy_chunk_budget.why_it_was_never_caught: The key was declared at plan time in config/cloudflare/phase-7-sprint-plan.json and read by nothing. No script under scripts/ computed a byte size of any collaboration module until this gate. CF-EV-P7-PERF-001 deferred the measurement to CF-P7-013 in as many words, and CF-P7-013 was the first time anyone looked.

options_weighed_before_the_decision.option: Renegotiate the budget on the record
options_weighed_before_the_decision.consequence: A decision-log entry raising 60 to a number the current shape meets, with the reason. Cheapest, and it concedes the 60 was never derived from a measurement. The gate would then enforce the new number instead of this record.

options_weighed_before_the_decision.option: Add a build step and meet the declared 60
options_weighed_before_the_decision.consequence: Minification and/or bundling of js/collaboration/*. The only route that makes the shipped bytes smaller rather than the target larger. It is a change to how the whole app is built and would invalidate the byte-for-byte artifact assertions Phase 1 established; it needs its own story and its own gate.

Load the eight panel surfaces on demand rather than through one entry closure. Keeps both the budget and the no-build property, at the cost of more dynamic imports and a second latency step the sprint's UX criteria never asked for.

What this manifest records. The breach stays visible here, in the exit report section 6.2, and in the risk register as R-P7-B, and it keeps open_defect on the Phase 7 zero-tolerance list unsatisfied, which is one of the reasons P7-G5 is not granted.

closed_open_items.was: document-envelope.js and storage-provider.js are deliberately outside the entry closure and answer 200 text/html on the deployment, the exact signature of the 037fb093 artifact defect. Nothing gates the first commit that imports either.
closed_open_items.closed_by: validateDeploymentArtifact now asserts the artifact's own import closure is complete: every relative specifier in every shipped .js resolves to a file the artifact contains. It runs inside build-pages.mjs and check-deployment-boundary.mjs, so it covers the artifact however it was assembled rather than trusting the build script that assembled it.
closed_open_items.found_while_closing_it: The residual risk was real but the mechanism recorded for it was not the whole story. Writing the gate exposed that build-pages.mjs's own specifier pattern matched `from '...'` and `import('...')` but not a bare `import './x.js';` -- a module reached only by a side-effect import was left out of the artifact while the build reported success. Verified by adding one to entry.js: before the fix the module was absent from _site, after it is present. Both patterns are now the same expression, so the set the gate asserts is present is the set the build decides to include.
closed_open_items.verified: Three ways, on the real artifact: a clean build passes; a hand-broken artifact whose entry imports a module that is not there is rejected with the offending edge named; and the previously-missed side-effect form is now followed by the build and caught by the gate.
